construct.constructDefinition: Professional engagement: teacher self-positioning on digital-competence maturity statements. Preserves each competence’s A1–C2 statement and separate zero-point not-aware response; not an agreement scale, a teaching-quality measure or an observed performance test. No area/global aggregate is computed by this split unit.

population.populationNotes: Adult primary and secondary teachers able to understand the fixed English Toolkit. Initial digital split scope; age18+ is a project scope, not a source-derived validation cut-off. Source studies do not establish Chinese-language or separate-area digital equivalence. Early-years use on the current website is not borrowed as validation for this fixed primary/secondary version.

administration.timeFrame: Current professional digital practice and experience; no fixed day/week recall period.
layoutConstraints: Choose the ONE original maturity statement that best describes your current competence in each item. Six item-specific A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2 statements are scored1–6, and the seventh not-aware response is scored0.
Keep the original competence order and original option order; no agreement anchors, automatic reversal, simplified alternatives or shortened items.
Six separate native area units are project packaging; independent administration equivalence is not established. The ordinary-composite recipe retains all32 competences in order.
This unit reports each competence separately; no area mean, global192-point total or overall A1–C2 band is manufactured across the split tools.

Missing items remain null; 0 is a real not-aware answer, not missing data. Any unanswered competence makes this area incomplete and suppresses its interpretations; this complete-area policy is a project choice, not an inferred source missing-data algorithm.
Timing is an approximate project allocation of the official circa25-minute whole-tool estimate, not measured timing.

intendedUses.notes: Professional learning self-reflection using a fixed EU source, not a certification, teacher appraisal or observed competence test.
Separate-area digital packaging and local applicability require explicit interpretation limits; not automatic cross-language/role equivalence.

options.label: A1: I am aware that digital technologies can be used for organisational communication (e.g. email, instant messaging, social networks, and online learning platforms).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies to help me communicate with colleagues, learners and/or parents (e.g. email, instant messaging, social networks, online learning platforms).
B1: I use various digital technologies according to my organisational communication needs (e.g. the communication goal, target and context).
B2: I analyse and select digital technologies based on their features and suitability for my organisational communication needs (e.g. effective, efficient and personal communication).

C1: I support and provide advice to colleagues on how to use digital technologies for organisational communication (e.g. for effective, efficient, safe, responsible, inclusive communication at school level).
C2: I contribute to developing organisational practices on communication using digital technologies (e.g. for effective, efficient, safe, responsible, inclusive communication).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that when managing online learning environments, ethical issues and use appropriate data management methods should be considered (e.g. open or restricted access, GDPR compliance).

A2: I have tried different settings to ensure that online learning environments to comply with ethical considerations and data management strategy (e.g. protection of users' data, access policy, terms of use, data management, privacy issues).
B1: I administer online learning environments in line with ethical considerations and data management strategy (e.g. administration features, managing content and student data).

B2: I analyse the features of online learning environments and apply the ones that best respond to the ethical considerations and data management strategy of my working context (e.g. security, users and data management, access policy, hosting of data).

C1: I support and provide advice to colleagues on ethical considerations and data management practices when using an online learning environment (e.g. use of passwords, encryptions, security procedures, data management transparency).
C2: I initiate and promote a school level data policy and code of ethical conduct in online learning environments (e.g. personal data management, accessibility for all, security, privacy).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that digital technologies can be used for collaboration and interactions with colleagues and/or other education stakeholders (e.g. exchange content by email attachments).

A2: I have tried using digital technologies to collaborate and interact with colleagues and/or other education stakeholders (e.g. exchange content using online services, participate in online professional networks).
B1: I use various digital technologies to collaborate and interact with colleagues and/or other stakeholders, according to collaboration needs (e.g. sharing content, practices, and/or ideas).

B2: I analyse and select digital technologies based on their features and how they can support collaboration tasks I need to engage in with colleagues and/or other education stakeholder (e.g. collaborative online activities).

C1: I lead collaborative tasks with colleagues and/or other education stakeholders using digital technologies (e.g. collaboration and co-creation of learning designs, implementation of joint projects).

C2: I initiate and promote collaborative activities between my school and its wider community using digital technologies (e.g. networks, communities and synergies, partnerships with local and wider community).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware of digital technologies available in my school that can support my professional practice (e.g. devices, applications, infrastructure).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies available in my school that can support my professional practice (e.g. interactive whiteboards, tablets, intranet).
B1: I use various digital technologies available in my school according to my professional practice needs (e.g. learning management system, cloud services).

B2: I analyse and select digital technologies available in my school based on their features and suitability to enhance my professional practice (e.g. online learning environments, immersive technologies).

C1: I support and provide advice to colleagues on how to use digital technologies available in our school for their professional practice (e.g. giving presentations, organising workshops, developing learning resources).
C2: I propose new digital technologies for professional practice to be used in my school (e.g. emerging technologies, applications, infrastructure).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that reflecting on how I use digital technologies can enhance my professional practice (e.g. online diary, peer-to-peer reflections).
A2: I have tried reflection methods on my use of digital technologies to further develop my digital competence (e.g. online self-reflection tools, reflection diary, digital story telling).
B1: I use various reflection methods in order to improve and update my professional digital practice (e.g. co-teaching, video recording of lessons, peer-debriefing sessions)

B2: I analyse the outcomes of my reflection to improve the use of digital technologies in my professional practice (e.g. analysing peer feedback, using mind mapping tools and other tools that support annotations, audio commentaries, online diaries).

C1: I support and provide advice to colleagues about improving the use of digital technologies in their professional practice through critical reflection (e.g. through discussion forums, blogs, social networks, online professional communities).

C2: I initiate and contribute to the development of a reflective learning culture that enhances the use of digital technologies in my school and beyond (e.g. lesson study, collaborative learning design, coaching, mentoring).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that my digital activity may have implications for my own reputation and that of my school (e.g. sharing private information, using inappropriate language)
A2: I recognise possible risks and threats for my reputation and that of my school relating to my digital activity (e.g. privacy, personal data, bullying, misinformation).
B1: I use mitigating measures to maintain a positive digital profile (e.g. understanding the provided terms of use, tracing my digital footprint, managing my privacy settings).

B2: I analyse and assess my digital footprint to adjust my behaviour and to help curate my own reputation online and that of my school (e.g. tracing my digital footprint, managing my privacy settings, blocking suspicious content and people, applying school guidelines on digital activities).
C1: I support and provide advice to colleagues on creating and curating ethical and responsible digital profiles (e.g. presentations, workshops, supporting material, activities).

C2: I initiate and promote school-level strategies that encourage staff and students to contribute positively, responsibly and ethically in a digital world (e.g. provide transparent data and content management procedures, develop an ethics code of conduct).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that digital technologies can support and enhance my professional learning (e.g. digital tools and resources, online learning environments and courses).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies for my professional learning (e.g. search for information online, join online courses, use online learning apps, visit online libraries and repositories).
B1: I use various digital technologies for my professional learning (e.g. discussions in a forum, uploading material, giving and taking feedback, presenting).
B2: I analyse and select online learning resources and activities that best suit my learning needs (e.g. webinars, online interactive courses, online learning communities).
C1: I support and provide advice to colleagues on using digital technologies for their professional learning (e.g. online learning communities, online repositories, e-portfolios).

C2: I initiate and promote a plan to support my colleagues’ digitally-enhanced professional learning (e.g. provide webinars, online training, online communities, resources repository, digital badges).
I am not aware of this competence.

A1: I am aware that engaging in professional learning activities on using digital technologies can develop my digital competence (e.g. webinars or workshops on the use of digital technologies in teaching and learning).

A2: I have attended professional learning activities about using digital technologies in order to develop my digital competence (e.g. micro-teaching, workshops on the use of digital technologies in teaching and learning).

B1: I participate in various formal and informal professional learning activities about using digital technologies to develop my digital competence (e.g. hands-on training on the pedagogical use of digital technologies, online learning approaches, digital assessment).

B2: I analyse and select professional learning activities about using digital technologies based on my needs (e.g. use a self-reflection tool on my digital competence, set learning goals, design my learning, reflect on my learning).

C1: I provide learning activities about using digital technologies and support colleagues on the development of their digital competence (e.g. workshops, informal sessions with colleagues, microteaching on the use of digital technologies).

C2: I contribute to the design of professional learning programmes which aim at developing teachers' digital competence (e.g. project-based learning with the use of digital technologies, digitally-enhanced learning design, exchange of good practices).
I am not aware of this competence.

A1: I am aware of computational thinking concepts and processes and how these relate to digital competence (e.g. analysing a problem to find a solution, recognising aspects of computational thinking around us).

A2: I have tried using computational thinking processes to explore solutions to a problem (e.g. decomposition of a problem, solution through a definition of steps, analysing a set of instructions applied to a solution).
B1: I use various digital tools to explore solutions to a problem following computational thinking processes (e.g. visual programming tools, authoring tools and editors).
B2: I analyse and select responses generated by algorithms (e.g. rank of search results, advertisements, how a robot can respond).
C1: I lead computational thinking activities in my school to support the development of colleagues’ and students’ digital competence (e.g. programming classes, competitions, hackathons).
C2: I contribute to the design and development of educational digital applications (e.g. games, mobile apps, assessment tools, customisation of virtual environments).
I am not aware of this competence.

items.content: 1.1. Professional engagement - Organisational communication Using digital technologies to enhance communication with colleagues and/or learners and/or parents.
1.2. Professional engagement - Online learning environments Managing online learning environments taking data management and ethics into account.
1.3. Professional engagement - Professional collaboration Using digital technologies to engage in collaboration and interactions with colleagues and/or other education stakeholders.

1.4. Professional engagement - Digital technologies and school level infrastructure Using digital technologies (devices, platforms and software) and infrastructure (internet access,local network) available in my school to enhance education.
1.5. Professional engagement - Reflective practice Reflecting on my own and collective professional practice with the use of digital technologies.
1.6. Professional engagement - Digital life Contributing positively and ethically in the digital world, considering safe and responsible digital practices.
1.7. Professional engagement - Professional learning (through digital technologies Using digital technologies for one's own professional learning.
1.8. Professional engagement - Professional learning (about digital technologies) Engaging in professional learning activities for the development of teachers’ digital competence.
1.9. Professional engagement – Computational thinking Engaging with computational thinking concepts and processes as part of teacher digital competence.

interpretations.headline: Reflecting on competence 1.1
interpretations.summary: This response records the maturity statement you selected for this specific digital competence. The statements describe awareness, exploration, use, purposeful selection, reflective support and wider initiative in item-specific ways. A higher point value indicates a later self-described position in this framework; it does not establish better teaching or better student outcomes. The separate not-aware response is a valid starting point for learning. Use a recent example and your working conditions to put the choice in context. The displayed points preserve the original statement order: 0 = not aware; 1 = A1; 2 = A2; 3 = B1; 4 = B2; 5 = C1; 6 = C2. These codes are maturity statements within this framework, not agreement levels, teacher grades or population percentiles.

limitations: Fixed source: 2022 Toolkit Annex I for complete item text and A1–C2 labels; official2023 report p.11/Annex1 for seventh not-aware option and0–6 point mapping. The2023 report omits the B2 row for6.5; no omitted row was invented.
These are self-reported digital-competence positions, not observed teaching, student learning outcomes, professional certification, personality labels or a school/teacher ranking.

The six separate digital area units, instructions, feedback and conservative missing policy are project adaptations. Current online text, independent-area validity and Chinese-version validity were not established.

Missing answers remain null and are not treated as a zero-point not-aware response. Any missing competence makes this area invalid/incomplete for interpretation. Other area units have their own completeness; no missing value is imputed. This project policy is not claimed as an author-issued missing-data algorithm.

No area average, global192-point score, overall proficiency band, population norm, percentile or cross-tool total is supplied. Consult the official Toolkit and2023 report for original glossary and full-tool interpretation.
report.disclaimer: For supportive professional learning reflection by the teacher receiving their own authorized results. A1–C2 are this framework’s maturity codes, not grades for teacher quality. No EU endorsement, badge or certificate is issued. Existing access and feedback permissions still apply.

instruction.text: Reflect on your current professional digital practice. For each competence choose the ONE statement that best describes your current position. A1, A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 are progressive, item-specific statements; they are not agreement ratings. If appropriate, choose “I am not aware of this competence”, which is a real zero-point answer. A missing response remains missing. This digital unit is one area of the fixed2022 SELFIEforTEACHERS Toolkit and uses the official per-item0–6 mapping described in2023. Feedback is for your professional learning, not teacher appraisal, EU certification or student-outcome prediction.
instruction.source: Project-written digital instruction grounded in JRC129699 Toolkit self-reflection navigation/AnnexI and JRC131282 p.11/Annex1; not a verbatim official platform instruction.
